messages:
incident-bot: SEV-2 paging: abnormal KV prefix growth + latency cliff observed for generation routes (multiple customers). Alerting on >1.5M prefix keys and 95th latency spike > 2s.

incident-bot: links: https://infra.redwood/alerts/1802345600, runbook: https://wiki.redwood/kv-cache-incidents

sara_oncall: ack. I'm on it — standing up triage. @mike_runtime @raj_ml please join if available.

mike_runtime: on call. grabbing logs now. quick hypothesis: continuous-batching change last night might be generating many unique prefix keys for templated prompts.

elaine_support: FYI we've seen CustomerA and CustomerB report slow responses and partial completions since ~08:45 UTC. Support routing is fielding inbound.

raj_ml: looking at model-usage traces — prompt templates for a small cohort got a new interpolation step in deploy c2f3b9 (templates-service). That change inserts a zero-width non-joiner when optional slot empty -> different tokenization and new prefix hashes.

mike_runtime: confirmed. quick grep on prefix-keys shows a 4x increase in unique prompt-key namespace tied to templates-service user-template v2.

mike_runtime: tail of internal log snippet (sanitized):
```
2026-03-15T08:42:11Z gen.srv: prefix_key="prompt_v2:u:12345:\u00A0" tokens=12 kv_lookup=MISS
2026-03-15T08:42:11Z kv.svc: prefix_namespace_count=2_120_431
2026-03-15T08:42:15Z scheduler: avg_inflight_tokens=52 target=8
2026-03-15T08:42:18Z perf: p95_latency_ms=2134
```

sara_oncall: impact: multiple production customers see high tail latencies, increased token cost due to low cache hits, and some 503s when batch queues overflow. Prioritize mitigation to reduce blast radius.

mike_runtime: mitigation plan (short): 1) disable continuous_batching on generation-prod route, 2) throttle max_batch_tokens to 256, 3) run targeted kv flush for affected prompt namespaces, 4) rollback template change if root cause confirmed.

raj_ml: if templates-service committed patch, rolling back is safest long-term, but that takes approvals. preferred immediate: flush and normalize keys + stop new divergent keys from being created.

sara_oncall: executing step 1 and 2 now.

mike_runtime: command I will run to restrict batching (dry-run first):
```
# reduce batch size and disable continuous batching for prod route
curl -s -X POST \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \
  https://admin.redwood/api/route/configure \
  -d '{"route":"generation-prod","continuous_batching":false,"max_batch_tokens":256}'
```

mike_runtime: done. verified config change propagated to 3/3 zones. Observed immediate drop in avg_inflight_tokens to ~10 in 30s.

ops-bot: config-change event recorded: route=generation-prod, actor=mike_runtime, tx=cfg-9f7a.

elaine_support: customer updates: CustomerA reports some improvement; partial completions still happening for long prompts. Support is holding customers to be notified when resolved.

sara_oncall: next: targeted kv flush. Need safe command and confirmation that flush will not evict valid warm prefixes. @mike_runtime can you prepare list of affected prefixes (pattern)?

mike_runtime: gathering. pattern = prompt_v2:user:*:\u00A0 and prompt_v2:template:* (the NBSP suffix). Will run with a dry-run count first.

mike_runtime: dry-run counts: prompt_v2:user:*\u00A0 -> 1_140_221 keys; prompt_v2:template:*\u00A0 -> 630_412 keys.

raj_ml: note: we must keep prompt_v2 without NBSP untouched — those are valid warm entries. Flush only NBSP-tagged keys.

mike_runtime: running flush in small windows to avoid thundering — shard by hash-range and 30s sleep between shards. Command:
```
POST /admin/kv/flush_prefix
{"prefix":"prompt_v2:","filter":"\u00A0","shard_range":"0-7"}
```

mike_runtime: flush started.

20m later...

mike_runtime: flush complete for all shards. cleared ~1.77M NBSP-suffix keys. cache hit-rate jumped from 22% -> 78% on affected routes. p95 latency down to ~380ms.

elaine_support: CustomerA and B report major improvement, CustomerC still sees edge cases on very long prompts.

sara_oncall: rolling back templates-service change c2f3b9 to prevent new NBSPs from being generated. Coordinating with deploy team.

raj_ml: deploy rollback in progress — note: the fix should also include sanitizing template interpolator to strip invisible whitespace; I'll open PR with tests for tokenization parity.

ops-bot: deploy event: templates-service rollback tx=deploy-4a2b by sara_oncall — started.

1h later...

mike_runtime: rollback completed, no new NBSP keys observed in logs. continuous_batching remains disabled for now.

sara_oncall: handing off to daytime oncall @raj_ml for follow-up and RCA. final status for now: latency mostly restored, cost reduced, customers informed. Marking incident as mitigated.

raj_ml: copying immediate action items: [1] PR to sanitize templates interpolator + unit tests for tokenization parity (owner: raj_ml), [2] add server-side validation to block control chars in template slots (owner: mike_runtime), [3] postmortem draft and customer impact summary for CS to send (owner: elaine_support).

elaine_support: I'll draft customer-facing note and send to PD/Legal for review. ETA 6h.

sara_oncall: retrospective note: consider adding canary for template engine changes that asserts stable prefix hashes for a sample of production prompts. Also add alerting on sudden prefix-namespace growth rate (delta per 10m) to detect similar regressions earlier.

incident-bot: Incident mitigated. ticket: INC-2026-3487 created, follow-ups assigned.

raj_ml: logging follow-ups in the ticket, will own RCA and timeline. Good job team, nice quick mitigation flow. :thumbsup:

sara_oncall: closing my shift, leaving notes in the ticket for daytime. if anything regresses ping me.

mike_runtime: leaving continuous_batching disabled until next confidence rollout and adding a canary that exercises template permutations in staging.

elaine_support: closing support loop with customers after PR lands.

(reacts: :hourglass_flowing_sand: from sara_oncall, :white_check_mark: from raj_ml)
